In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the receptor for polyimmunoglobulin is synthesized in the rat liver during the first 2 weeks of life, but the secretory component is only secreted in the serum in significant amounts at the onset of weaning.
the ontogeny of secretory component in the liver follows a biphasic pattern.
the ontogenic expression by the liver of the receptor for the secretory component of IgA is a two-step process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ontogenic expression and processing of the receptor for secretory component in the liver are independent of hormonal and humoral factors and are initiated by weaning, while the magnitude of the production by the liver of secretory component, the receptor for secreted immunoglobulins, is under the control and regulation of glucocorticoid hormones.
the ontogenic expression and processing of the polymeric Ig receptor in the liver is a complex process involving both hormonal and developmental controls.
the ontogeny of the polymeric receptor is a multistep phenomenon that involves the expression of immature precursors during the suckling period and the appearance of a mature receptor at weaning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of the secretory component is regulated by a complex mechanism, which includes the synthesis, intracellular processing, and secretion of a receptor precursor.
the expression of the receptor and its precursors in rat hepatocytes during growth is regulated in a tissue-specific and age-dependent manner.
the ontogeny of the polymeric Ig receptor is a complex process, involving both the regulation of receptor synthesis and the regulation of its secretion.
